topIssues.title: feat(plugin): add Aomi on-chain execution integration
topIssues.author: phoebe-aomi
topIssues.body:
## Problem

Eliza agents can execute a fixed wallet surface, but they cannot delegate open-ended on-chain workflows to the Aomi agent backend while preserving elizaOS wallet custody and confirmation controls.

## Scope

Add `@elizaos/plugin-aomi` under `plugins/plugin-aomi` with:

- one `AOMI` action for natural-language on-chain requests;
- a long-lived service that maps Eliza rooms to Aomi sessions;
- planner context for Aomi availability and pending wallet requests;
- EVM, EIP-712, and Solana wallet-envelope execution through `@elizaos/plugin-wallet` only;
- a separate human confirmation turn before every signature or submission;
- stable action results, focused tests, package docs, configuration metadata, and registry metadata.

## Acceptance criteria

- Read-only Aomi requests complete without a wallet.
- A wallet-producing request returns a concrete preview and cannot sign or submit on the initiating turn.
- A later yes/no reply confirms or rejects the exact pending request.
- EVM transaction, EIP-712, Solana sign, Solana sign-message, and Solana submit envelopes use the configured wallet backend without reading private keys directly.
- Concurrent Eliza rooms remain isolated, and a room cannot start a second Aomi operation while one is pending.
- Package build, typecheck, lint, tests, live Aomi connectivity, a live-model trajectory, and testnet execution evidence are attached to the PR.

## Evidence plan

- Package build/typecheck/lint/test logs.
- Live `api.aomi.dev` read request and wallet-envelope flow.
- Live-model trajectory showing action selection, confirmation, and completion.
- Testnet transaction hash, explorer link, wallet balance before/after, and signed-payload trail.
- Failure-path evidence for rejection, invalid configuration, and RPC/submission failure.
- UI screenshots/video: N/A — backend plugin with no rendered UI.

topIssues.title: fix: repair current develop verification contracts on Windows and UI
topIssues.author: lalalune
topIssues.body:
## Problem

Current `develop` at `d44bd7577f33a1de90814b4d5633835ce7da4a43` has deterministic verification defects:

- the shared i18n bootstrap compares a native Windows argv path to a hand-built `file://` URL and therefore does not execute when invoked directly;
- Bun JUnit evidence emits native `\` separators on Windows while the repository inventory is POSIX-normalized, so identical test files do not reconcile;
- `ElizaClient.getModelsCatalog()` passes an explicit second `undefined` argument, breaking the established one-argument fetch contract and the current Client test;
- `@elizaos/import-conversations` and `@elizaos/logger` use POSIX-only `find | xargs` pipelines for TypeScript lint/format discovery, so the Windows exhaustive lane either fails before Biome or accidentally scans byte-preserved JSON fixtures;
- `@elizaos/capacitor-gateway` launches `bash` to probe SwiftLint, which invokes the Windows WSL stub and aborts root verification even though its installed `node-swiftlint` wrapper already owns platform detection.

These are independent of the remaining document/scenario/PA and external Hetzner failures and should be repaired without broad workflow weakening.

## Acceptance criteria

- Direct-run detection uses Node URL/path primitives and is proven with encoded Windows-compatible paths plus a real child-process generator invocation.
- JUnit suite and testcase identities normalize native separators before strict inventory comparison; missing, duplicate, and mismatched identities still fail closed.
- Models-catalog fetch preserves the one-argument call when no `RequestInit` is supplied and forwards a supplied signal/options object unchanged.
- TypeScript-only Biome discovery is implemented once with Node filesystem/process primitives, excludes declarations and adjacent fixtures exactly as before, and is exercised through both affected package scripts on Windows.
- Native Gateway lint invokes `node-swiftlint` through its package script on every host: the wrapper runs real SwiftLint on macOS when installed and returns an explicit platform skip elsewhere, without Bash/WSL probing.
- Focused tests, Biome, root typecheck/lint verification, and current-base diff checks pass.

## Evidence

Attach command output to the PR. UI screenshots/video: N/A — no rendered behavior changes; this repairs invocation, evidence-path, lint-discovery, native-tool orchestration, and request-call contracts only.

Medium. This adds a wallet-capable external agent integration. The implementation
fails closed for unsupported EVM batches, never reads signing keys directly,

# Background

## What does this PR do?

- Adds first-party `@elizaos/plugin-aomi` and its generated registry entry.

- Routes explicit Aomi prompts to a single `AOMI` action.
- Supports read-only Aomi tasks without credentials through the public
  `https://api.aomi.dev` default app.
- Previews and confirms single-call EVM transactions, EIP-712/personal
  signatures, Solana transactions, and Solana message signatures.
- Retains executed wallet results across failed Aomi callbacks so a retry cannot
  broadcast twice.
- Includes publish-ready 400x400 logo and 1280x640 banner assets.

![Aomi plugin banner](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/phoebe-aomi/eliza/codex/aomi-plugin/plugins/plugin-aomi/images/banner.jpg)

confirmation behavior, development checks, and opt-in live tests.

# Testing

then `service.ts` for room isolation/idempotency and `wallet.ts` for the custody

topPRs.title: fix(cloud): make agent backup scheduling durable
topPRs.author: lalalune
topPRs.body:
## Summary

Progresses #15783 by replacing process-local backup scheduling assumptions with a durable, generation-fenced database lane.

- reserves due backups with database time and `FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED`
- fences attempts to the exact job claim and sandbox image generation
- prevents a late/reclaimed worker from marking a newer image healthy
- records absent, stale, unsupported, unreachable, repeated-failure, and backlog pressure states distinctly
- deduplicates fleet incidents and verifies non-2xx alert delivery
- caps alert claims to the visible actionable batch so truncated rows remain alertable
- makes snapshot execution fail closed behind `ELIZA_SNAPSHOT_JOBS_ENABLED`

## Why this is not a timer-only patch

The failure mode crosses scheduler, queue, image lifecycle, worker recovery, and operator health. This PR gives those boundaries durable identities and compare-and-swap transitions. A backup only advances freshness when the executing job still owns the exact attempt and image generation it started against; clock skew and stale worker completion cannot fabricate health.

## Verification

Re-run after rebasing onto current `develop`:

- `bun --conditions=eliza-source test packages/cloud/shared/src/db/repositories/agent-sandbox-backup-health.test.ts packages/cloud/shared/src/lib/services/provisioning-jobs-scheduled-backup-sentinel.test.ts packages/cloud/shared/src/lib/services/provisioning-worker-health-monitor.test.ts packages/scripts/cloud/admin/daemons/provisioning-worker.backup-fleet-health.test.ts packages/scripts/cloud/admin/daemons/provisioning-worker-env-reconcile.test.ts` — 63 passed, 0 failed (Windows-only verbatim GNU-shell cases skip by design)
- `bun run --cwd packages/cloud/shared typecheck` — passed
- `git diff --check origin/develop...HEAD` — passed

The implementation audit also passed the full sandbox lifecycle (159 passed, 6 platform skips), 16 real PGlite repository tests, and 145 focused tests before the final rebase.

## Evidence matrix

- Real DB concurrency/CAS: covered by the PGlite suite above
- Backend state/logs: deterministic repository and daemon tests above
- UI screenshots/video: N/A — no user-facing UI change
- Real LLM trajectory: N/A — no model/action/prompt behavior
- Production fleet/RPO evidence: pending protected staging rollout and soak

## Explicit remaining gates

This stays draft and does **not** close #15783 yet:

1. Prepared workflow wiring for the protected `ELIZA_SNAPSHOT_JOBS_ENABLED` variable could not be pushed: the available OAuth token lacks `workflow` scope, the GitHub App cannot write repository contents, and no SSH key is configured. The exact patch is posted separately for a maintainer with workflow authority.
2. Staging must enable the lane, prove backup age/coverage and restore viability over the required soak, then production needs protected-variable sign-off.
3. Retention/R2 deletion remains owned by #17172/#17180/#17214 and is intentionally not duplicated here.

The runtime defaults the snapshot lane off, so merging without the protected rollout wiring cannot silently activate it.

topPRs.title: fix(personal-assistant): gate private context by audience
topPRs.author: 0xSolace
topPRs.body:
## Summary

R2 replaces the blocked R1 design. Shaw's two reviews were correct.

- normalize stored room type and message channel type to an authoritative audience **class**; `DM`, `SELF`, `VOICE_DM`, and `API` are private surfaces
- enforce one shared private-context retrieval boundary across `lifeOpsProvider`, `crossChannelContextProvider`, `pendingApprovalsProvider`, and `calendarAction`
- bind provenance inside that boundary to the loader-derived persisted Agent identity (`runtime.getAgent(runtime.agentId)`), never mutable `character.name` or message persona text
- capture a deterministic room/membership version at retrieval and re-read it at final output, calendar callbacks, and every streamed model chunk
- remove the unreachable public-group inclusion model from this private-loader boundary
- report authorization/DB/loader failures through `runtime.reportError`, fail closed, and expose explicit unavailable states rather than fabricated healthy zero counts

## Production regression fixed

The compatibility API ingress really does persist `type: ChannelType.DM` in `ensureCompatChatConnection` while web/OpenAI/Anthropic messages stamp `channelType: ChannelType.API` (`packages/agent/src/api/chat-routes.ts`). R1's exact equality check returned empty owner context on that production path.

R2 classifies both values as `private`, while still requiring the persisted room, owner requester, agent participant, and exact owner+agent audience. The PGlite production-path matrix covers persisted `DM` + message `API`, `DM` + `VOICE_DM`, `DM` + `DM`, and `SELF` + `SELF`.

## Shared retrieval and delivery boundary

- All four private disclosure surfaces call `authorizeLifeOpsPrivateContext` before constructing/loading private data.
- The authorization envelope is attached to the production message and tracked for streaming.
- `outgoing_before_deliver` revalidates authoritative room type and participants and replaces the payload with a safe cancellation response if the audience changed.
- `model_stream_chunk` revalidates before each chunk. Core now honors mutating stream hooks before any client callback, structured extractor, or downstream stream path sees the chunk.
- Calendar action callbacks call the same delivery assertion before invoking transport callbacks.

## Production-path evidence

The integration test uses the real PGlite `AgentRuntime`, persisted Agent/room/entity/participant records, real exported provider entrypoints, the real calendar action handler, and the real core pipeline hook registry. The stale-audience test mutates the DB participant set after private retrieval authorization and before final delivery; the private canary is replaced before the delivery callback. A core runtime test drives the real `AgentRuntime.useModel` streaming path and proves a denied mutating hook prevents every downstream chunk callback.

## Tests

- `bunx vitest run --config vitest.src-integration.config.ts src/lifeops/audience-policy.integration.test.ts` (from `plugins/plugin-personal-assistant`) — **10 passed**
- `bunx vitest run packages/core/src/runtime/__tests__/model-stream-chunk-hooks.test.ts` — **6 passed**
- `bunx @biomejs/biome check <9 changed TypeScript files>` — **passed**
- `node packages/scripts/run-turbo.mjs run typecheck --concurrency=4 --filter=@elizaos/core --filter=@elizaos/plugin-personal-assistant` — **79/79 tasks passed**, including both package typechecks

Rebased onto `develop` at `626b884d` before the R2 commit.
